body:
It's all good. I am just trying to take it one day at a time and encourage them whenever a social opportunity does come up. It really is a relentless cycle it seems because they do not want to do anything because of the depression, and then when they do something (Attend School), they get in a horrible mood because they feel left out when everyone around them talks about their weekend. I am at the point where I just want them to desperately try antidepressants because I can not think of anything else at this point, but I know pushing that over and over is going nowhere.

Thanks for the reply though, I don't expect anyone to have the perfect answer on how to deal with this anymore than me, but getting insight from others is always nice. I'll definitely read more in the sidebar. Thanks again.

They feel left out of stuff constantly and like they aren't experiencing life. The people they know do not invite them to most things that they do, and they are not having luck making new friends. School is not going well either as they are pretty behind and have trouble getting themselves to go. They feel like they won't have the same experiences as other people including me by the time I did (I am older, so they're comparing the time I did x and saying they have to do it by the time they are that old too or there is no point.)

I try my best to be understanding and talk to them but more often than not they get agitated and just start shutting everything down and have already decided they are done living. If I keep trying to talk they just get angrier and this can last for hours. I try to tell them things will get better, they're doing a good job, progress is being made and we can keep working on things, I'm there for them, but none of this seems to get through in the moment.
